rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen says she will wait for the envoys' return.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فناظرة ﴾ فمنتظرة ﴿ بم ﴾ أي بما لأن الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here بَم means بِما; the alif is deleted after a preposition in an interrogative.
rows.anchor: أي بما لأن الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She waits to see whether the envoys return with the gift accepted or rejected, knowing royal custom: a king accepts and departs, while a prophet rejects it and demands adherence to his religion.
rows.anchor: لأنها عرفت عادة الملوك وحسن مواقع الهدايا عندهم فان كان ملكا فبلها وانصرف وان كان نبيا ردها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The queen sent a lavish, elaborately dressed party of five hundred boys and five hundred girls, gold and silver bricks, a jeweled crown, a pearl, and a crooked-hole bead, led by al-Mundhir ibn Amr.
rows.anchor: فبعثت خمسمائة غلام عليهم ثياب الجواري وحليهن راكبي خيل مغشاة بالديباج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her letter challenged Solomon, if he was a prophet, to distinguish the boys from girls, identify the container's contents, pierce the pearl, and thread the crooked bead; she told the leader to judge his reaction.
rows.anchor: وقالت فيه أن كنت نبيا فميز بين الوصفاء والوصائف وأخبر بما في الحق واثقب الدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon staged a grand display with gold and silver paving, animals, jinn, humans, and other creatures; the envoys threw down the gifts when they saw animals soil the precious paving.
rows.anchor: فأمر سليمان الجن فضربوا لبنات الذهب والفضة وفرشوها في ميدان بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon smiled, solved the pearl and bead tests with an insect and a white worm carrying thread, tested the envoys with water to distinguish boys from girls, and returned the gift.
rows.anchor: فأمر الأرضة فاخذت شعره ونفذت في الدرة وأخذت دودة بيضاء الخيط بفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger who came to Solomon was the queen's envoy al-Mundhir ibn Amr.
rows.anchor: رسولها المنذر بن عمرو

rows.speaker: مكي وسهل ومدني وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Makki and Sahl retain the yāʾ in both pause and connection; Madani and Abu Amr agree in connected reading, with two nūns.
rows.anchor: بنونين واثبات الياء في الوصل والوقف مكي وسهل وافقهما مدني وأبو عمرو في الوصل

rows.speaker: حمزة ويعقوب وغيرهم
rows.claim: Hamza and Yaqub read أتمدوني with yāʾ in both cases; the remaining readers use two nūns without yāʾ in either case.
rows.anchor: أتمدوني حمزة ويعقوب في الحالين وغيرهم بنونين بلا ياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is directed to the envoys.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God gave Solomon means prophethood, kingship, and blessing.
rows.anchor: من النبوة والملك والنعمة

rows.speaker: مدني وأبو عمرو وحفص
rows.claim: Madani, Abu Amr, and Hafs read the yāʾ in آتاني with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وبفتح الياء مدني وأبو عمرو وحفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What the queen's people were given means worldly ornaments and luxury.
rows.anchor: من زخارف الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadīya names the thing given, and it can be attributed either to its giver or to its recipient, just as ʿaṭiyya names what is bestowed.
rows.anchor: الهدية اسم المهدي كما ان العطية اسم المعطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon says God's gifts to him are better: religion brings the greater benefit and sufficiency, and he already has ample worldly goods, so he needs no financial support.
rows.anchor: أن ما عندي خير مما عندكم وذلك أن الله آتاني الدين الذي فيه الحظ الأوفر والغنى الأوسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The envoys rejoice in gifts because they know only outward worldly life; Solomon will accept nothing but faith and abandoning Magianism.
rows.anchor: بل أنتم قوم لا تعلمون إلا ظاهرا من الحياة الدنيا فلذلك تفرحون بما تزادون ويهدى إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With wa, Solomon would presume the addressees know his greater wealth; with fa, he treats them as unaware, informs them of his state, and objects to their offer as unnecessary.
rows.anchor: إذا قلته بالواو وجعلت مخاطبي عالما بزيادتي في الغنى وهو مع ذلك يمدني بمال وإذا قلته بالفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift with بل moves from rejecting and explaining the offer to naming its cause: the envoys know no grounds for joy beyond worldly gain.
rows.anchor: أنه لما أنكر عليهم الامداد وعلل إنكاره أضرب عن ذلك إلى بيان السبب الذي حملهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-taqaṭahu means that Pharaoh's people took the child.
rows.anchor: أخذه قال الزجاج كان فرعون من أهل فارس

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Pharaoh was Persian, from Istakhr.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج كان فرعون من أهل فارس من اصطخر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes the outcome as the sense: they did not take Moses in order to make him their enemy; events came to that end, as in the saying about a child being born for death.
rows.anchor: قاله الزجاج وعن هذا قال المفسرون ان هذه لام العاقبة والصيرورة

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators call the lām the lām of consequence or eventual outcome.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون ان هذه لام العاقبة والصيرورة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashshāf calls it a purpose lām, but says its causal sense is figurative because the outcome of their taking him resembles a motive for it.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب الكشاف هي لام كي التي معناها التعليل كقولك جئتك لتكرمني ولكن معنى التعليل فيها وارد على طريق المجاز

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads the alternate form ḥuzn; both forms are Arabic variants, like the two forms of ʿadam.
rows.anchor: وحزنا على حمزة وهما لغتان كالعدم والعدم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar lightens the hamza in the reading of khāṭiʾīn.
rows.anchor: خاطين بخفيف خاطئين أبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were sinners, and God punished them by raising their enemy and eventual destroyer in their own household; their wrongdoing in everything made this outcome typical of them.
rows.anchor: أي كانوا مذنبين فعاقبهم الله بان ربي عدوهم ومن هو سبب هلاكهم على أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one Moses meant to strike was the Copt, described as hostile to Moses and the Israelite either because he did not share their religion or because the Copts were enemies of Israel.
rows.anchor: لموسى والإسرائيلي لأنه ليس على دينهما أو لأن القبط كانوا اعداء بني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite spoke, mistakenly thinking Moses meant to seize him rather than the Copt, after Moses had called him plainly astray.
rows.anchor: الإسرائيلي لموسى عليه السلام وقد توهم أنه أراد أخذه لا أخذ القبطي إذ قال له إنك لغوي مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here jabbār means a killer who acts in anger.
rows.anchor: أي قتالا بالغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The land meant is Egypt.
rows.anchor: ﴿ في الأرض ﴾ أرض مصر

words: وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite accuses Moses of not wanting to be among those who restrain their anger.
rows.anchor: في كظم الغيظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killing was widely known, but the killer had been concealed; the Israelite's words revealed Moses to the Copt, who informed Pharaoh and prompted the plot to kill him.
rows.anchor: أن قاتله موسى فأخبر فرعون فهموا بقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man was the believer from Pharaoh's family, and Pharaoh's cousin.
rows.anchor: هو مؤمن آل فرعون وكان ابن عم فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasʿā can be an adjective for rajul or a circumstantial clause; rajul already has the modifier from the city's outskirts.
rows.anchor: صفة لرجل أو حال من رجل لأنه وصف بقوله من أقصى المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders either urge one another to kill Moses or deliberate and consult about him; iʾtimār is mutual counsel, with each person advising the other.
rows.anchor: أي يأمر بعضهم بعضا بقتلك أو يتشاورون بسببك والائتمار التشارو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man urges Moses to leave the city.
rows.anchor: من المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase laka clarifies the counsel rather than modifying nāṣiḥīn, since a relative complement cannot precede its antecedent; it is like saying 'welcome to you.'
rows.anchor: لك بيان وليس بصلة الناصحين لأن الصلة لا تتقدم على الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses left the city in fear, watching for an attack on the road or someone pursuing him to kill him.
rows.anchor: التعرض له في الطريق أو أن يلحقه من يقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unjust people Moses asks to escape are Pharaoh's people.
rows.anchor: أي قوم فرعون

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's denial of knowing another god can imply that no other god exists for them, or be taken literally as saying no other god is known to him.
rows.anchor: قصد بنفي علمه باله غيره نفى وجوده أي مالكم من إله غيري أو هو على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks Haman to bake clay into bricks and build with them; this phrasing is apt because Pharaoh is said to be the first brickmaker and it teaches the craft.
rows.anchor: أي اطبخ لي الآجر واتخذه وأنما لم يقل مكان الطين هذا لأنه أول من عمل الآجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Haman by name in the middle of the command, and ordering him to fire the clay, sounds eloquent and tyrannical, signaling Pharaoh's arrogance.
rows.anchor: ولأنه أفصح وأشبه بكلام الجبابرة إذ أمر هامان وهو وزيره بالايقاد على الطين منادي باسمه بيافي وسط الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣarḥ is a high palace or building.
rows.anchor: قصرا عاليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṭṭaliʿ means to ascend; iṭṭilāʿ is climbing upward.
rows.anchor: أي أصعد والاطلاع الصعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh imagined that God occupied a place, as Pharaoh himself did.
rows.anchor: حسب أنه تعالى في مكان كما كان هو في مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh calls Moses a liar for claiming to have a god who sent him as a messenger.
rows.anchor: في دعواه أن له إلها وأنه أرسله إلينا رسولا

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh contradicts himself: he first denies any god but himself, then asks Haman for help and admits Moses has a god, while conceding he is not certain Moses lies.
rows.anchor: وقد تناقض المخذول فإنه قال ما علمت لكم من إله غيري ثم أظهر حاجته إلى هامان وأثبت لموسى إلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous report says Haman gathered fifty thousand builders for an unprecedented tower; Gabriel struck it apart, killing a million of Pharaoh's soldiers with one section, while the others fell into the sea and west, and every worker died.
rows.anchor: روى أن هامان جمع خمسين ألف بناء وبنى صرحا لم يبلغه بناء أحد من الخلق فضرب الصرح جبريل عليه السلام بجناحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners they are told to invoke are the idols, called upon to rescue them from punishment.
rows.anchor: أي الأصنام لتخلصكم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols did not answer those who called on them.
rows.anchor: فلم يجيبوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to law is omitted; the implied completion is that they would not have seen the punishment.
rows.anchor: وجواب لو محذوف أي لما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qārūn is indeclinable because it is a foreign proper name; if it were a native faʿūl form from qarana, it would decline.
rows.anchor: لا ينصرف للعجمة والتعريف ولو كان فاعولامن قرنت الشيء لانصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was an Israelite and Moses' cousin, from the line of Levi; he was called al-Munawwar for his beauty, knew the Torah better than the Israelites, but became a hypocrite like al-Samiri.
rows.anchor: كان اسرائيليا ابن عم لموسى فهو قارون بن يصهر بن قاهث بن لاوى بن يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghā means that Qarun transgressed and oppressed his people.
rows.anchor: من البغي وهو الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported explanations say Pharaoh appointed Qarun over Israel and he oppressed them; alternatively, his wealth and children made him arrogant, or he wore clothes a handspan longer than theirs.
rows.anchor: قيل ملكه فرعون على بني اسرائيل فظلمهم أو من البغي الكبر تكبر عليهم بكثرة ماله وولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is a relative pronoun in the accusative as the object of ātaynāhu; the following inna clause is its relative clause, explaining the kasra on inna.
rows.anchor: ما بمعنى الذي في موضع نصب بآيتنا وأن واسمها وخبرها صله الذي ولهذا كسرت إن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mafātiḥ can mean keys or treasuries, depending on the vowel of the singular maftaḥ; the author prefers the sense 'keys'.
rows.anchor: والمفاتح جمع مفتح بالكسر وهو ما يفتح به أو مفتح بالفتح وهو الخزانة والأصوب أنها المقاليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keys weigh down the large group; the bā makes the verb transitive, as in the idiom for a load weighing someone down until he leans.
rows.anchor: لتثقل العصبة فالباء للتعدية يقال ناء به الحمل إذا أثقله حتى أماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keys were carried by sixty mules, one key per treasury; each key was no larger than a finger and made of leather.
rows.anchor: وكانت تحمل مفاتيح خزائنه ستون بغلا لكل خزانة مفتاح ولا يزيد المفتاح على اصبع وكانت من جلود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ulū al-quwwa means people of strength.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أولي القوة ﴾ الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'when his people said' is grammatically accusative in relation to tanūʾ.
rows.anchor: ومحل إذ نصب بتنوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speakers were either the believers or Moses.
rows.anchor: أي المؤمنون وقيل القائل موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means not to exult arrogantly over wealth; the author compares it with the prohibition in 57:23.
rows.anchor: لا تبطر بكثرة المال كقوله ولا تفرحوا بما آتاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only someone content and settled in worldly life rejoices in it; a person whose heart looks to the Hereafter knows this world will soon be left behind.
rows.anchor: ولا يفرح بالدنيا إلا من رضي بها واطمأن وأما من قلبه إلى الآخرة ويعلم أنه يتركها عن قريب فلا يفرح بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fariḥīn here means those who are arrogant and boastful about their wealth.
rows.anchor: البطرين بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Use the wealth and abundance God gave you to seek the Hereafter through charity to the poor, maintaining kinship, and other good works.
rows.anchor: بأن تتصدق على الفقراء وتصل الرحم ونصرف إلى أبواب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view is to take from this world what suffices and benefits you.
rows.anchor: وهو أن تأخذ ما يكفيك ويصلحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is to use worldly means to attain the Hereafter, which is the believer's share of this world.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه وأطاب بدنياك آخرتك فإن ذلك حظ المؤمن منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do good to God's servants; alternatively, show gratitude and obedience to the Creator for His beneficence.
rows.anchor: أو أحسن بشكرك وطاعتك لخالق الأنام كما أحسن إليك بالإنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking corruption in the land means acting unjustly and transgressing.
rows.anchor: بالظلم والبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thing Qarun claims he was given is wealth.
rows.anchor: أي المال

rows.speaker: قارون
rows.claim: Qarun claims his wealth came through merit based on knowledge that distinguished him from other people, with possible meanings including Torah knowledge, alchemy, or expertise in trade and farming.
rows.anchor: أي على استحقاق لما في من العلم الذي فضلت به الناس وهو علم التوراة أو علم الكيمياء

rows.speaker: قارون
rows.claim: The author also lists knowledge of commercial and agricultural methods as Qarun's possible claim to have earned the wealth through his own expertise.
rows.anchor: أو العلم بوجوه المكاسب من التجارة والزراعة وعندي صفة لعلم

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says no one prospers by admiring himself: the fortunate person sees God's favor in every deed and word, while the wretched person boasts of his own actions and is destroyed by that conceit, as Qarun was.
rows.anchor: قال سهل ما نظر أحد إلى نفسه فأفلح والسعيد من صرف بصره عن أفعاله وأقواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the question as affirming that Qarun knew from the Torah that God had destroyed earlier people stronger and richer than him, yet failed to learn from their fate.
rows.anchor: هو إثبات لعلمه بأن الله قد أهلك من القرون قبله من هو أقوى منه وأغنى لأنه قد قرأه في التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the question denies Qarun had this useful knowledge: despite claiming superior knowledge and deserving every favor, he did not recognize the fate of the earlier powerful generations.
rows.anchor: أو نفى لعلمه بذلك لأنه لما قال أوتيته على علم عندي قيل عنده مثل ذلك العلم الذي ادعاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More abundant in collected wealth, or greater in followers and numbers.
rows.anchor: للمال أو أكثر جماعة وعددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Possible explanations: God already knows their sins, so they enter without reckoning; they confess without questioning; their marks identify them, though they may still be questioned in rebuke; or the verse concerns criminals of this community not being asked about earlier peoples' sins.
rows.anchor: لعلمه تعالى بهم بل يدخلون النار بغير حساب أو يعترفون بها بغير سؤال أو يعرفون بسيماهم فلا يسألون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Qarun opposed Moses, resented the zakat assessment, and persuaded the Israelites that Moses meant to take their property; he then paid a prostitute to accuse Moses of sexual misconduct.
rows.anchor: كان قارون يؤذي موسى عليه السلام كل وقت وهو يداريه للقرابة التي بينهما حتى نزلت الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the festival Moses announced punishments for theft, false accusation, and illicit sex; when Qarun engineered an accusation against Moses, the woman confessed that Qarun had paid her, and Moses prayed to God while prostrating.
rows.anchor: فقالت جعل لي قارون جعلا على أن أقذفك بنفسي فخر موسى ساجدا يبكي وقال يا رب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses command over the earth; it swallowed Qarun and his companions progressively to their necks and then closed over them as they pleaded with Moses, who remained angry.
rows.anchor: فقال يا بني اسرائيل إن الله بعثني إلى قارون كما بعثني إلى فرعون فمن كان معه فليلزم مكانه

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: In the account, God tells Moses that Qarun had sought his help repeatedly without receiving mercy, and swears that a single appeal to God would have been answered with mercy.
rows.anchor: فقال الله تعالى استغاث بك مرار فلم ترحمه فوعزتي لو استرحمني مرة لرحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When some Israelites suspected Moses had destroyed Qarun to inherit his property, Moses prayed to God, and the earth swallowed Qarun's house and treasures too.
rows.anchor: فدعا الله حتى خسف بداره وكنوزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiʾa means a group.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فما كان له من فئة ﴾ جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No group could protect Qarun from God's punishment.
rows.anchor: يمنعونه من عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muntaṣirīn can mean those who take revenge on Moses or those who defend themselves against God's punishment; naṣara and intasara describe helping against an enemy and thereby resisting him.
rows.anchor: من المنتقمين من موسى أو من الممتنعين من عذاب الله يقال نصره من عدوه فانتصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibrahim may be accusative after an implied adhkur, with إذ قال as a genitive apposition of inclusion; it may instead coordinate with Noah or be a time adverb for God's sending him when he was ready to preach.
rows.anchor: نصب باضمار أذكر وأبدل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, إذ قال is a time adverb for 'We sent him': Ibrahim was sent when his age or knowledge qualified him to exhort his people.
rows.anchor: أو ظرف لأرسلنا يعني أرسلناه حين بلغ من السن أو العلم مبلغا صلح فيه لأن يعظ قومه

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi and Abu Hanifa read Ibrahim in the nominative, meaning 'and among the messengers was Ibrahim.'
rows.anchor: وقرأ إبراهيم النخعي وأبو حنيفة رضي الله عنهما إبراهيم بالرفع على معنى ومن المرسلين إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and fear God; doing so is better for you than unbelief, if you know what benefits and harms you.
rows.anchor: إن كان لكم علم بما هو خير لكم مما هو شر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awthān means idols.
rows.anchor: ﴿ إنما تعبدون من دون الله أوثانا ﴾ أصناما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhluqūn can mean that they lie and fabricate, or that they make things.
rows.anchor: وتكذبون أو تصنعون

rows.speaker: أبو حذيفة والسلمى
rows.claim: Abu Hudhayfa and al-Sulami read the form from khalaqa, conveying multiplying or making abundantly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حذيفة والسلمى رضي الله عنهما وتخلقون من خلق بمعنى التكثير في خلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afkan is also read; it is a verbal noun like lying or playing, while ifk is its shortened form, as kadhib and laʿib are shortened from their roots.
rows.anchor: وقرىء أفكا وهو مصدر نحو كذب ولعب والافك مخفف منه كالكذب واللعب من أصلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabrication is calling idols gods and partners of God.
rows.anchor: واختلافهم الافك تسميتهم الأوثان آلهة وشركاء لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot provide their worshippers any sustenance; God alone is the provider, so they should seek provision from Him.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيعون أن يرزقوكم شيئا من الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship and thank God for His blessings, preparing to meet Him, since you will return to Him.
rows.anchor: فاستعدوا للقائه بعبادته والشكر له على أنعمه

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub reads the t with fatḥa and the jīm with kasra, an active form meaning 'you return.'
rows.anchor: وبفتح التاء وكسر الجيم يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting the road means killing and taking property, as highway robbers do.
rows.anchor: بالقتل وأخذ المال كما هو عمل قطاع الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that they intercepted travelers to commit sexual wrongdoing against them.
rows.anchor: وقيل اعتراضهم السابلة بالفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nādī means an assembly or meeting place, and is called a gathering only while its people are present.
rows.anchor: مجلسكم ولا يقال للمجلس ناد إلا مادام فيه أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned public acts include flatulence, sex, insults and obscenity in joking, flicking pebbles, chewing gum, finger-snapping, and using a toothstick among people.
rows.anchor: أي المضارطة والمجامعة والسباب والفحش في المزاح والحذف بالحصى ومضغ العلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of answering Lot, his people demanded God's punishment if he was truthful about its coming.
rows.anchor: فيما تعدنا من نزول العذاب

rows.speaker: شامي وحفص
rows.claim: The Shami readers and Hafs read the opening with two hamzas, as in the canonical codex.
rows.anchor: أئنكم شامى وحفص وهو الموجود في الإمام وكل واحدة بهمزتين

rows.speaker: كوفي غير حفص
rows.claim: The Kufis other than Hafs lengthen the hamza and follow it with a kasra yāʾ.
rows.anchor: كوفي غير حفص آينكم آينكم بهمزة ممدودة بعدها ياء مكسورة

rows.speaker: عمرو ومكي ونافع غير قالون وسهل ويعقوب غير زيد
rows.claim: The passage assigns the shortened-hamza form followed by a kasra yāʾ to Amr and the named Makki, Nafiʿ, Sahl, and Yaqub readers, with the stated exceptions.
rows.anchor: أو عمرو أينكم أينكم بهمزة مقصورة بعدها ياء مكسورة مكي ونافع غير قالون وسهل ويعقوب غير زيد

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recite the revealed Book to draw near to God and learn its commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: تقربا إلى الله تعالى بقراءة كلامه ولتقف على ما أمر به ونهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establish the prayer means to maintain it regularly.
rows.anchor: أي دم على إقامة الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḥshāʾ means a vile deed, such as fornication.
rows.anchor: الفعلة القبيحة كالزنا مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munkar is what religious law and reason condemn.
rows.anchor: هو ما ينكره الشرع والعقل

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: When told of a man who prayed by day but stole at night, the Prophet said that his prayer would restrain him.
rows.anchor: فقال إن صلاته لتردعه

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: A young Anṣārī who prayed with the Prophet yet committed every kind of indecency was described to him; he said the man's prayer would stop him, and the young man soon repented.
rows.anchor: أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي معه الصلوات ولا يدع شيئا من الفواحش إلا ركبه

rows.speaker: ابن عوف
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAwf explains that while one is praying, one is engaged in obedience and held back from indecency and evil.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عوف أن الصلاة تنهى إذا كنت فيها فأنت في معروف وطاعة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says a prayer that does not restrain its performer from indecency and evil is not prayer, but a burden against that person.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن من لم تنهه صلاته عن الفحشاء والمنكر فليست صلاته بصلاة وهي وبال عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that prayer surpasses other acts of worship because it is remembrance of God; the wording supplies this reason for its superiority.
rows.anchor: أي الصلاة أكبر من غيرها من الطاعات وإنما قال ولذكر الله ليستقل بالتعليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's remembrance of people through mercy is greater than their remembrance of Him through obedience.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ولذكر الله إياكم برحمته أكبر من ذكركم اياه بطاعته

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭā says God's remembrance is greater because it is without cause and does not end, while human remembrance is mixed with motives and wishes and does not last.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء ذكر الله لكم أكبر من ذكركم له لأن ذكره بلا علة وذكركم مشوب بالعلل والأماني

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman says remembrance of God is better than anything; he cites the Prophet calling it better than the best deeds, charity in gold and silver, or fighting an enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال سلمان ذكر الله أكبر من كل شيء وأفضل فقد قال عليه السلام ألا أنبئكم بخير أعمالكم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says the best deed is to leave this world while one's tongue remains moist with remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: وسئل أي الأعمال أفضل قال أن تفارق الدنيا ولسانك رطب بذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are that God's remembrance exceeds the grasp of minds, is greater than committing sin alongside it, or restrains indecency and evil more than anything else.
rows.anchor: أو ذكر الله أكبر من أن تحويه أفهاكم وعقولكم أو ذكر الله أكبر من أن تلقى معه معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the good and obedience people do and rewards them.
rows.anchor: من الخير والطاعة فيثيبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards those deeds with the finest reward; this fragment completes the prior segment's explanation of His knowledge and recompense.
rows.anchor: العنكبوت ( 49 - 46 ) أحسن الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God originates creation by bringing created beings into existence.
rows.anchor: الله يبدأ الخلق ﴾ ينشئهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God restores creation by reviving people after death.
rows.anchor: يحييهم بعد الموت

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وسهل
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Sahl read the verb with yāʾ rather than tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبالياء أبو عمرو وسهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAmad is the plural of ʿimād, a pillar or support.
rows.anchor: جمع عماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the heavens. The phrase can stand independently as evidence that they are visibly unsupported, or modify ʿamad as 'pillars that are not seen'; the latter means God holds the heavens by His power.
rows.anchor: الضمير للسموات وهو استشهاد برؤيتهم لها غير معمودة على قوله بغير عمد كما تقول لصاحبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading with unseen pillars, the heavens are sustained by God's power even though their supports are not visible.
rows.anchor: يعنى أنه عمدها بعمد لا ترى وهو امساكها بقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawāsi are fixed, stable mountains.
rows.anchor: جبالا ثوابت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains were placed so that the earth would not shake with you.
rows.anchor: لئلا تضطرب بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baththa means to scatter and spread abroad.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وبث ﴾ ونشر ﴿ فيها من كل دابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means a kind or species.
rows.anchor: من كل زوج ﴾ صنف ﴿ كريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karīm means good or fine.
rows.anchor: صنف ﴿ كريم ﴾ حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hādhā points to the created things just mentioned.
rows.anchor: اشارة إلى ما ذكر من مخلوقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq Allah here means God's created work or creatures.
rows.anchor: أى مخلوقه

words: فَأَرُونِى مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge exposes the idolaters: God made these tremendous things, so they should show what their gods created to deserve worship.
rows.anchor: يعنى آلهتهم بكتهم بأن هذه الأشياء العظيمة مما خلقه الله فأرونى ما خلقته آلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse shifts from exposing their failure to declaring that the wrongdoers are mired in manifest error.
rows.anchor: أضرب عن تبكيتهم إلى التسجيل عليهم بالتورط فى ضلال ليس بعده ضلال

rows.speaker: مدني والباقون
rows.claim: Madani reads mithqālu in the nominative, with the pronoun referring to the story; the other readers use the accusative, taking the pronoun as the deed of wrong or right.
rows.anchor: بالرفع مدنى والضمير للقصة وأنث المثقال لإضافته إلى الحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative reading makes kāna a complete verb; in the accusative reading it is copular and the pronoun refers to the act of good or evil, as small as a mustard seed.
rows.anchor: والباقون بالنصب والضمير للهيئة من الإساءة والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites an unnamed poetic line as evidence for feminine agreement when the masculine noun is annexed to the feminine word ḥabba.
rows.anchor: كما قال كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a tiny deed hidden in a rock's core or anywhere in the upper or lower world will be brought by God; most interpreters identify the rock with Sijjīn, where evil deeds are recorded, outside the earth.
rows.anchor: أى فكانت مع صغرها فى أخفى موضع وأحرزه كجوف الصخرة أو حيث كانت فى العالم العلوى أو السفلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings the deed forth on the Day of Resurrection and holds its agent to account.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة فيحاسب بها عاملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laṭīf means either that God's knowledge reaches every hidden thing or that He is gentle in extracting it; Khabīr means He knows its true nature or its location.
rows.anchor: عالم بكنهه أو لطيف باستخراجها خبير بمستقرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admission that God alone created the heavens and earth entails that praise and thanks belong to Him alone and that no one else should be worshipped with Him.
rows.anchor: الزام لهم على اقرارهم بأن الذى خلق السموات والأرض هو الله وحده وأنه يجب ان يكون له الحمد والشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most do not understand that this admission binds them to worship God alone, and fail to notice when reminded.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك يلزمهم واذا نبهوا عليه لم يتنبهوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God.
rows.anchor: لله ما في السماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghanī means God has no need of those who praise Him.
rows.anchor: عن حمد الحامدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥamīd means that God deserves praise even if people do not praise Him.
rows.anchor: المستحق للحمد وان لم يحمدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists claimed revelation would run out; God answers that His words cannot be exhausted.
rows.anchor: قال المشركون ان هذا أى الوحى كلام سينفد فأعلم الله أن كلامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if every earthly tree became pens and the ocean, supplied by seven more seas, became ink, God's words would not run out; compare 18:109.
rows.anchor: ولو أن اشجار الأرض أقلام والبحر ممدودا بسبعة أبحر وكتبت بتلك الاقلام وبذلك المداد كلمات الله لما نفدت كلماته

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Amr and Yaqub read al-baḥr in the accusative, coordinated with mā after inna; the nominative can follow the syntactic position of inna and its clause or make al-baḥr an initial clause with a circumstantial wāw.
rows.anchor: والبحر بالنصب أبو عمرو ويعقوب عطفا على اسم أن وهو ما والرفع على محل أن ومعمولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading of yمده is also reported.
rows.anchor: وقرىء يمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than say 'the sea is ink,' the verse says it is supplied: the great sea is like an inkwell continually filled by seven seas that never run dry.
rows.anchor: وكان مقتضى الكلام أن يقال ولو ان الشجر أقلام والبحر مداد لكن أعنى عن ذكر المداد قوله يمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajara is singular to describe the trees one by one, until not a single tree remains unshaved into pens.
rows.anchor: وانما ذكر شجرة على التوحيد لأنه أريد تفصيل الشجر وتقصيها شجرة شجرة حتى لا يبقى من جنس الشجر ولا واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural of paucity kalimāt is preferred over the plural of abundance kalim to stress that even the seas cannot suffice to write God's words, let alone one word.
rows.anchor: وأوثر الكلمات وهى جمع قلة على الكلم وهى جمع كثيرة لأن معناه ان كلماته لا تفى بكتبتها البحار فكيف بكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzīz means that nothing can overpower God.
rows.anchor: لا يعجزه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥakīm means nothing falls outside God's knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: لا يخرج من علمه وحكمته شيء
